identity.coverageNote: Selected source ligament surface. Attachments and adjoining spaces require specialist review. Recovered from the v4 source in its unchanged common coordinate frame. Independent anatomical review is pending.

mri.title: Check ligament of right lateral rectus · MRI orientation · draft
mri.body: Orient along the lateral rectus toward the lateral orbital wall. Human histology shows sleeve extensions attaching to periosteum; this provides an anatomic context for the lateral check ligament, not proof that its individual fibers can be resolved on routine MRI.
bullets: The lateral check ligament concerns the lateral rectus fascial support. Do not substitute the visible muscle belly or the superior-rectus–lateral-rectus band for the ligament itself.

The Atlas mesh is an anatomic reference, not an acquired MRI or patient-to-Atlas registration. Small fascial structures may be lost to acquisition resolution and partial-volume averaging; absence on a slice is not evidence of absence in the orbit.

No individual check-ligament MRI visibility or diagnostic performance is established here. The orbital-apex tendon has disputed detailed boundaries in cadaver studies; do not infer them from the mesh or a single MR slice.
mri.note: Revision-bound radiologist review pending. No scan, patient registration, diagnostic finding or clinical approval is supplied. Atlas, imaging-case and lecture access remain independent.

mri.title: Check ligament of right medial rectus · MRI orientation · draft
mri.body: Orient along the medial rectus toward the medial orbital wall. Human histology shows fine connections from its thick sleeve to periosteum; these are anatomic support structures, not an MRI-validated separately visible target.
bullets: The medial check ligament is associated with medial rectus fascia, away from the lateral rectus support and from the apical common tendinous origin.
